The main takeaway from our work is that
, if the size of the final grammar(s), or grammars in a vacillating class, is to be bounded by a small constant, the learning power of the resulting model of learning is severely restricted.
, for the classes of languages that we consider, the learning power of vacillating between n grammars is essentially the same as the learning power of a single grammar of size at most n.

, in the context of a certain natural class of grammars and languages, the restriction of the final grammar(s)'s size to be small is not a significant limitation on the learning power of vacillating learners.
